 Putnam Health Department offers holiday food and cooking safety tips
 November 11, 2026 
 9:22 am 
 Mid-Hudson News Staff 
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 LinkedIn 
 Email 
 Print 
 MHNN file photo 
 BREWSTER- With the holiday cooking season approaching, the Putnam County Department of Health is reminding residents to take precautions to prevent foodborne illness, kitchen accidents, and cooking fires.
 Health officials stress four basic food safety steps: clean, separate, cook, and chill. Residents should wash their hands with soap and water for at least 20 seconds, keep raw meats away from cooked and ready-to-eat foods, and properly refrigerate leftovers.
 Frozen turkeys and other meats should be thawed in the refrigerator, cold water or microwave—not on the countertop. Officials also advise against washing raw turkey, which can spread harmful bacteria around the kitchen. Turkey should be cooked to an internal temperature of 165 degrees, checked with a food thermometer in three places. Stuffing should reach the same temperature.
 Cooking safety is equally important. Residents are urged to never leave stovetops unattended, keep flammable items away from cooking areas and maintain a three-foot safety zone around hot surfaces for children and pets. Thanksgiving is the leading day of the year for cooking fires, according to the National Fire Protection Association.
 The department also warns against using open-flame turkey fryers, which pose serious fire hazards.
 Officials encourage residents to take a few extra precautions so holiday celebrations can be remembered for good food and family gatherings rather than food poisoning, injuries or fires.
